issues.offendingText: assertAspect(canvas, cw / ch);
issues.problem: Both assertAspect calls are tautological: they compare the canvas's aspect against the exact values just used to size that canvas (captureFullFrame asserts videoWidth/videoHeight against a canvas sized from videoWidth/videoHeight; captureWysiwyg asserts cw/ch against cw/ch). As written the dev assert can never fail, so it cannot catch the CSS-pixel-sizing regression it claims to guard.
issues.fix: Assert against an independently derived expectation: in captureFullFrame compare canvas aspect to the track's getSettings() aspect; in captureWysiwyg compare canvas aspect to the preview box aspect (boxAspect), with a tolerance for integer rounding.

issues.offendingText: PayoutInstruction.status runs `pending` (batch building), `issued` (in an exported file or accepted by the partner), then `succeeded` or `failed` (payouts.mdx)
issues.problem: Three incompatible PayoutInstruction status enums: phase-1/payouts.mdx uses pending → issued → succeeded|failed; spec/state-machines.mdx (which says 'the states below are derived here and are canonical') uses pending → dispatched → paid|failed|cancelled; spec/data-model.mdx CHECK-pins a third set ('pending','exported','executing','paid','failed','returned','cancelled') and marks it 'Defined here'. THESIS defines only the pin_ prefix, not the states, so the spec pages must agree and they do not.
issues.fix: Adopt state-machines' enum (pending, dispatched, paid, failed, cancelled) as canon. In payouts.mdx replace `issued`→`dispatched` and `succeeded`→`paid` everywhere (truth table, repair loop, Done means). In data-model.mdx rewrite the payout_instructions CHECK to ('pending','dispatched','paid','failed','cancelled') and drop 'exported','executing','returned'; update the partial-index WHERE clause accordingly.

issues.offendingText: An instruction keeps its id across retries, incrementing `attempt` and re-pointing `batch_id` (state-machines.mdx)
issues.problem: Contradictory instruction-identity semantics: spec/state-machines.mdx says a failed instruction is re-queued (failed → pending, same pin_ id, attempt++); phase-1/payouts.mdx says 'Instructions are immutable attempts: repair creates a new instruction on the same claim'; spec/api.mdx /payout-instructions/{pin_id}/reissue says 'a new instruction on the same claim in the next batch'; spec/data-model.mdx's partial unique index ('A failed or returned instruction releases the partial unique index, so a later batch can cut a fresh instruction') also assumes new rows. An implementer cannot satisfy both audit models.
issues.fix: Pick the immutable-attempt model (3 of 4 pages, and it matches the data-model index design): in state-machines.mdx delete the failed→pending re-queue transition and the attempt/batch_id re-pointing sentence; replace with 'reissue creates a new PayoutInstruction (new pin_) on the same claim in a new building batch, audit instruction.reissued linking both'.

issues.offendingText: `building` | both | Finance adds approved claims; instructions `pending`; member claims remain `approved` (state-machines.mdx)
issues.problem: When does a claim become in_payout? phase-1/payouts.mdx: 'Adding a claim to a `building` batch moves it from `approved` to `in_payout`' (and its truth table shows building/pending/in_payout); end-to-end-flow.mdx step 11 agrees ('each claim flips to `in_payout`' at batch build). spec/state-machines.mdx says claims remain `approved` while building and only move at export/execute ('A batch leaves `building` | Member claims move to `in_payout`'). Opposite transitions on the same edge.
issues.fix: Decide once: recommend the state-machines version (in_payout only when the batch leaves building; while building the claim is reserved-but-approved). Then fix payouts.mdx ('Adding a claim... reserves it; it moves to in_payout when the batch is exported/executed; removing while building releases the reservation') and e2e step 11 plus its master-table `approved`/`in_payout` rows to match. Alternatively flip state-machines; either way all three pages must name the same edge.

issues.offendingText: Breach | 48h | 24h | step `escalated`; successor for backup or delegate ... Second breach ... step `expired` (approval-engine.mdx)
issues.problem: ApprovalStep escalated/expired semantics are reversed between pages. phase-1/web/approval-engine.mdx: first SLA breach → `escalated` (successor created), `expired` = 'escalation ladder exhausted without a decision' (parks in admin queue); end-to-end-flow echoes this ladder. spec/state-machines.mdx: SLA breach → `expired`, then `expired` --escalate--> `escalated` with successor. THESIS lists both statuses without ordering, so the two pages define opposite machines for the same enum values.
issues.fix: Align state-machines.mdx to the approval-engine/e2e semantics: active --SLA breach--> `escalated` (successor step for backup/delegate/admin, fresh clock); `escalated`-chain exhausted --> `expired` (terminal marker, claim parks in admin queue). Update the ApprovalStep ASCII diagram and the two transition rows accordingly, and keep approval-engine's status table as-is.

issues.offendingText: Failed payout repair | ... claim returns to the `approved` pool flagged `payout_failed` (end-to-end-flow.mdx)

issues.fix: Amend end-to-end-flow.mdx gate-one paragraph: capture, upload, drafting and field review work at zero balance; pre-submission OCR pauses (receipts hold in `queued`); the max(20, 3 × remaining credits) fair-use cap applies only while the balance is positive — mirroring credits-and-metering's sentence.

Then propagate it: add the changed-inputs re-resolve branch to the state-machines `sent_back`→`submitted` transition guard and soften e2e's 'the original policy snapshot still governs' to 'unless amount increased or routing inputs changed, in which case the chain re-resolves'.

issues.fix: Make rule-schema's behavior canonical (it is the spec page and matches 'Rule selection uses the evaluation instant'); reword e2e's loop row to: 'rules re-evaluate at resubmission; the routing chain resumes per the approval-engine rules'. Keep snapshot language scoped to chain/config, not rule evaluation.
